problem: A coffee shop tracks how often customers order a latte. On average, $30%$ of customers order a latte. Each customer’s order is independent of the others. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability that the first customer who orders a latte is at least the $4$th customer is{{field-1}}.

feedback.problem: A board game uses a special deck of $10$ cards: $4$ cards show a star and $6$ cards show a circle. A player randomly draws a card, records the symbol, and then puts the card back into the deck before drawing again. The player keeps drawing until they get a star card. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability of getting a star card after the third draw is{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of cards drawn until a star card is obtained. The chance of selecting a star card from the deck is 

$$
p=\frac{4}{10}=\frac{2}{5}=0.4.
$$

So, the number of selections before obtaining a star card can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success $p=\frac{2}{5}.$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(\frac{2}{5}).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={(1-\frac{2}{5})}^{x-1}(\frac{2}{5}) \\  & ={(\frac{3}{5})}^{x-1}(\frac{2}{5})\end{aligned}
$$

To compute $P(X>3),$ we will use the complement:

$$
P(X>3)=1-P(X\le 3)
$$

Computing the probability of the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & =P(X\in {1,2,3}) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3) \\  & ={(\frac{3}{5})}^{1-1}(\frac{2}{5})+{(\frac{3}{5})}^{2-1}(\frac{2}{5})+{(\frac{3}{5})}^{3-1}(\frac{2}{5}) \\  & =(\frac{2}{5})+(\frac{3}{5})(\frac{2}{5})+{(\frac{3}{5})}^{2}(\frac{2}{5}) \\  & =[1+(\frac{3}{5})+{(\frac{3}{5})}^{2}](\frac{2}{5}) \\  & =[1+\frac{3}{5}+\frac{9}{25}](\frac{2}{5}) \\  & =0.784.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability of getting a star card after the third draw is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>3) & =1-P(X\le 3) \\  & =1-0.784 \\  & =0.216.\end{aligned}
$$
